knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The dog is moved away from the trigger and the group is kept under control. The walker does not force the dog past the bicycle or grab the collar.
The walk must stay within the lower limit that applies to any part of the route, which is four in this example.
The lesson says a dog on a lead must be under the walker's control at all times.

practicalCriteria: Assessor observes the candidate hold two simulated dogs on leads of suitable length with the leads not wrapped around the hand
Assessor presents a simulated trigger and observes the candidate move the dog away from it before a conflict starts
Assessor checks a route plan that applies the lowest council group limit to the whole route
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Route plan with the group limit recorded
Walk record for the simulated walk, with any incident noted
Temperament note check for the simulated dog
stopWorkCriteria: A dog is walked off-lead on public land where it is not under effective control
The walker places their hands between fighting dogs
The group exceeds the lowest applicable council limit
